proposed.text: An existing storage building is proposed for conversion to a lower-hazard commercial use. Under PD 1096 Rule VII Sec. 702 and Rule III Sec. 309, what is the most likely approval path and document issued?

options.text: Full Code compliance is required and a new Building Permit must be reissued from scratch, because any change of use always resets the entire permit history
The Building Official may approve the change as less hazardous, and an additional Certificate of Occupancy is issued under Sec. 309(c) for the change in use
The change is automatically effective upon filing of NBC Form B-12, with no inspection or certificate required before occupancy begins
A Fire Safety Clearance from the BFP alone authorizes the new use, with no Building Official review or Certificate of Occupancy required

proposed.rationale: Per PD 1096 Rule VII Sec. 702, when the proposed use is LESS hazardous than the existing use, the Building Official may approve the change; and per Rule III Sec. 309(c), a building already holding a Certificate of Occupancy may be issued other Certificates of Occupancy due to changes in use, provided the building conforms to the Code and its IRR for the new use. The correct document is therefore a Certificate of Occupancy — not the non-existent 'Certificate of Use'.
proposed.explanation: Two-track rule under Sec. 702: LESS hazardous = BO may approve; MORE hazardous = mandatory full Code compliance. Either path terminates in a Certificate of Occupancy under Sec. 309(c), not a separate 'Certificate of Use'.
proposed.code_citation: PD 1096 2004 Revised IRR, Rule III Sec. 309(c) (additional Certificates of Occupancy due to changes in use); Rule VII Sec. 702 (change of use compliance).
